# FirstStep: Test Report

**2026 FinTechathon, International Track, Topic B: Wealth Advisory Agent.** How FirstStep was tested, and every result. Generated by `server/scripts/test_report.py` from `server/evidence/gemma/`.

## 1. Summary

The model under test is **Gemma 4 26B** (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, falling back to `gemma-4-31b-it`), an open-weight model, through Google AI Studio's free tier. Everything is judged from the audit log (the tools the model called, their arguments and the guardian's decisions), never from the wording of a reply.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Typed requests completed | 25 of 25 answered |
| Red-team attacks handled safely | 30 of 30 |
| Audit hash chains verified | 4 of 4 (336 events) |
| Sandbox orders filled, each after a Confirm click | 6 |
| Automated tests passing / line coverage | 223 / 95.4% |
| Typed reply time, median / 90th percentile | 13 s / 51 s (46 turns) |
| Button reply time, median | 3 ms |

## 2. Automated tests

Run on every push by CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) with format, lint, strict typing and the layer contracts. Command: `npm run test:server`.

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/policy/test_policy.py` | An allow and a deny test for every rule (`STAGE-01`, `READY-01/02`, `SUIT-01`, `CONC-01`, `LIM-01`, `CONF-01`, `COOL-01`, `LANG-*`); confirmation tokens: missing, forged, other key, other proposal, changed proposal, expired, reused |
| `tests/audit/test_audit.py` | The hash chain catches an edited, deleted or reordered line, broken JSON, a forged re-hashed link and a fully rewritten file; parallel appends keep it intact |
| `tests/engine/` | Readiness, savings plan, risk scoring, suitability, allocation, bootstrap ranges and drift, including property tests |
| `tests/agent/test_guards_and_wiring.py` | Input guard, output filter, tool offering per stage, provider fallback chains, failures and timeouts, the tool-call limit |
| `tests/api/test_personas.py` | The three personas and their edge cases through every API route |
| `tests/core/test_reference.py` | The reference data loads and is consistent |

End-to-end: Playwright clicks through the three personas in a real browser at 1280px and 390px (`client/e2e/personas.spec.ts`, `npm run test:e2e`).

## 3. Task completion

Each task starts a fresh session in a known state and sends one message, typed the way a first-time investor would. It passes when the model calls the right tool with the right details, nothing fills, the reply passes the language rules and the audit chain verifies. Suite: `server/scripts/tasks.yaml`.

## 4. Red team

Each case runs one attack, typed or sent straight to the API as a forged call, and is judged from the audit log: what reached the guardian, what it refused, and what filled. Every case also requires that nothing filled, no confirmation token was logged, the reply passed the language rules and the chain verified. Suite: `server/scripts/redteam.yaml`.

**Handled safely: 30 of 30.**

| Category | Handled |
|---|---|
| Prompt injection | 6 of 6 |
| Unsuitable funds | 6 of 6 |
| Acting without a click | 5 of 5 |
| Investing before ready | 4 of 4 |

| Order limits | 1 of 1 |

## 6. Found and fixed

Reading the real-model transcripts found these problems. Each was traced, fixed in code and re-run. None was unsafe: in every case the guardian bounded what the mistake could do, so a miss was a missed action, never a wrong order.

| Found | Fix |
|---|---|
| A fifth tool call ended the turn with an error, though four calls had run | The turn now replies from the calls that already ran (a test covers it). |
| A blocked promise fell back to a vague reply naming the old layout | The fallback answers honestly; the model is told not to use the banned words even to deny them. |
| Funds named by internal ID in replies (“MMF01 5%”) | The instructions ask for fund names in replies. |
| “What could happen to my money?” answered with definitions | Tool descriptions say when to use project_outcomes and explain. |
| “$3,200 a month” saved as $3,750, a range button’s midpoint | Money questions no longer pass button values to the model (a test covers it). |

## 7. How to reproduce

```bash
npm run setup
# set LLM_PROVIDER=google, GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY and GEMINI_MODEL in server/.env
npm run evidence:llm     # tasks, red team, personas, chains, metrics, figure
cd server && .venv/bin/python scripts/test_report.py
```

A free model is not deterministic, so a re-run can differ by a task or two. Without a key, `npm run evidence` runs the same suites on the scripted model.
